exercises.instructions:
Create a Query that returns a product (id, code, description) and a Query that returns an order (id, totalAmount). Use #[SimpleObject].

No database yet: read the data from src/db/fixtures.rs, an in-memory copy of the database seed (e.g. get_product_by_code, get_order_by_id).

Add the OrderLine simple object and a custom resolver for Order.lines. Use #[ComplexObject].

The lines of an order come from fixtures::get_order_lines_by_order_id, and each line only knows its product_id: resolve the product with fixtures::get_product_by_id.

Extract each domain into its own file:
- products.rs: the Product type and a ProductQuery
- orders.rs: the Order type and an OrderQuery

From now on every exercise keeps this layout: start each one by copying the files of the previous exercise.

Enrich the domain model:

Add a status field as an Enum to Order, with values DRAFT, CONFIRMED and CANCELLED.

Add a Customer field (SimpleObject with id/name/vat).

Add a Money scalar (amount + currency) and use it for:
- Order.totalAmount (it was a Float until now)
- OrderLine.price
- OrderLine.discount (optional)

💡 Money is a scalar whose value is a JSON object ({"amount": 10.0, "currency": "EUR"}): implement ScalarType by hand, or derive serde on the struct and use the async_graphql::scalar! macro.

There is a lot of duplication into the query.

Put the common fields (id, code, description) into an Interface.

💡 Each field(name, ty) of the interface calls the method generated on the concrete type, and #[derive(SimpleObject)] getters return references: use ty = "&ID", or mark the field #[graphql(owned)] to declare ty = "ID". String fields can use ty = "String".

Make the test ex08 pass!

🧪 tests/ex08_one_of.rs

Split the monolith into two federated subgraphs (Federation v2), both reading from the database:

- products (src/ex09_federation/products.rs, port 3001): Query.product(code), Mutation.createProduct and the ProductKind interface with its implementations.
- orders (src/ex09_federation/orders.rs, port 3002): Query.order(id) with status, customer, totalAmount and lines.

Each module exposes `Query` (and products also `Mutation`) built with ::default(): see src/bin/09_products.rs, 09_orders.rs and 09_export-schemas.rs.

The only type shared by the two subgraphs is ProductKind:

1. In products, ProductKind becomes an entity interface: the interface and every type implementing it (Product, DangerousProduct, ExpiringProduct) need @key(fields: "id"). In async-graphql a type gets its @key from an entity resolver: add one #[graphql(entity)] method per type, taking `#[graphql(key)] id: ID`.
2. In orders, an OrderLine only knows the product id. Declare a ProductKind SimpleObject with just the id, mark it #[graphql(interface_object)] and add an entity resolver that builds it from the id. The router will ask the products subgraph for code, description and the specific fields.

Run it:

- `cargo make local` exports your SDL to schemas/09_*.graphql, composes the router config with wgc (composition errors show up here) and starts subgraphs + router on http://localhost:5000/graphql. Run it again after every change.
- Try the query with the `09 - federated order` request of the Postman collection (see the README).

📚 https://async-graphql.github.io/async-graphql/en/apollo_federation.html
📚 https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/schema-design/federated-schemas/entities/interfaces

Make the test ex09 pass!

🧪 tests/ex09_federation.rs

Strangler pattern: a new customers service takes over Customer.name from the orders subgraph, behind a feature flag.

- orders: Customer becomes an entity (@key on id).
- customers (port 3003): reads the customers table and overrides the name with #[graphql(override_from = "orders")].
- fake_customers: a base subgraph that only declares the Customer entity. In Cosmo a feature subgraph replaces an existing base subgraph: customers is published as the feature subgraph of fake_customers.

Follow the WunderGraph Federation part of `cargo make help` (Cosmo account required).

No account? `cargo make local-feature-flag` composes the same graph locally (schemas/federation/federation-compose-feature-flag.yaml) and starts a router on port 5000 that honors the X-Feature-Flag header. Try it with the `10 - feature flag customers` request of the Postman collection, with and without the X-Feature-Flag header.

📚 https://async-graphql.github.io/async-graphql/en/apollo_federation.html
📚 https://cosmo-docs.wundergraph.com/concepts/feature-flags

Make the test ex10 pass!

🧪 tests/ex10_feature_subgraph.rs

Every OrderLine resolves its product with its own query: an order with N lines costs N queries (N+1 problem).

Add a ProductLoader (DataLoader) that collects the product ids of the request and loads them with a single query: retrieve_products_by_ids in src/db/products.rs already does it.

OrderLine.product must go through the loader. Log the keys received by load() to see the batching.

📚 https://async-graphql.github.io/async-graphql/en/dataloader.html

Make the test ex11 pass!

🧪 tests/ex11_dataloader.rs

Apply DataLoader to the products subgraph of ex09: copy src/ex09_federation/products.rs into src/ex12_dataloader_federated/products.rs.

The router sends one _entities call with many representations, but async-graphql invokes the entity resolvers once per representation: N representations cost N queries.

Make every entity resolver go through a ProductLoader so that they are resolved by a single query. The test builds the loader itself, so ProductLoader needs two public fields: `pool` and `load_calls: Arc<AtomicUsize>`, to increment in every load() call.

The test sends the _entities request to the schema in-process: no Docker needed.

The key insight: federation's network batching is not database batching. You need a DataLoader inside each subgraph.

📚 https://async-graphql.github.io/async-graphql/en/dataloader.html

🧪 tests/ex12_dataloader_federated.rs

Query the ex09 federated graph from a typed Rust client using cynic.

The supergraph schema is in schemas/13_supergraph.graphql (generate it with `cargo make supergraph` if missing) and is registered in build.rs.

Implement fetch_order (query) and create_product (mutation with a @oneOf input) in src/ex13_cynic.

Don't write the structs by hand: generate them from schemas/13_order.graphql (order query, from tests/ex09_federation.rs) and schemas/13_create_product.graphql (createProduct mutation, from tests/ex08_one_of.rs):

- Web: https://generator.cynic-rs.dev (upload schemas/13_supergraph.graphql, paste the query)
- CLI:
  cargo install --locked cynic-cli
  cynic querygen --schema schemas/13_supergraph.graphql --query schemas/13_order.graphql
  cynic querygen --schema schemas/13_supergraph.graphql --query schemas/13_create_product.graphql

Then adapt the generated code to the test:
- Money is an object scalar ({amount, currency}): a serde struct + impl_scalar!
- DateTime maps to chrono::DateTime<Utc> (impl_scalar! as well)
- inputs use owned String fields, without lifetimes
- OrderStatus must derive PartialEq
- the schema module lives in src/ex13_cynic/mod.rs: `use super::schema;` in order.rs and create_product.rs
- type names must match the ones used by the test

Run `cargo make local` first (it starts the ex09 subgraphs).

📚 https://cynic-rs.dev/quickstart.html
